Abū Ḥayyān al-Tawḥīdī made this statement while answering a question from Ibn Saʿdān, the vizier of Ṣamṣām al-Dawla al-Buwayhī. The vizier had asked him about Zayd ibn Rifāʿa. From the question, we understand that Zayd had some connection with the vizier, attended his gatherings, and discussed many matters of learning and knowledge with him, but the vizier did not know what school or doctrine Zayd followed. The dialogue that Abū Ḥayyān records here is important for our subject. It shows how much uncertainty surrounded Zayd ibn Rifāʿa even among the educated people of his own time, and the vizier Ibn Saʿdān was one of them. Abū Ḥayyān’s discussion of the Brethren of Purity also shows that these educated contemporaries knew little about the group itself, even during the period when it is said to have appeared.↩︎

There is confusion here about the location of Alamut. In fact, the fortress stood in the region south of the Caspian Sea, not in Syria. —Publisher.
